title: Compact subspace supports joint eye/image decoding
key_values: selected hard-negative n128 feature posterior, pyramid_local_field k8 cosine with compact k10: zeroed-eye 0.765/0.668/0.576 at 0.5/1/2x; compact-only 0.850/0.838/0.826; compact-removed 0.759/0.635/0.537; full joint and compact-addback 0.872/0.872/0.871; known-trace control 0.927/0.936/0.949
claim: When eye position is latent, compact-only recovery retains much of full joint feature recovery, while compact removal collapses recovery toward the zeroed-eye curve.
claim_boundary: This is an absolute feature-posterior endpoint, not image-identity accuracy or a gain normalized to the moving zero-eye baseline. It supports compact-subspace necessity for this projection intervention, not that the animal computes the posterior, that the compact subspace is unique, or that behavior optimizes this objective. The known-trace row is a deterministic control, not an independent known-pose response target.
production_gate: Keep image-identity observer, posterior-Neff, source-contrast, motion-delta diagnostics, and static-PC/non-unique compact controls in caption/supplement.
